turn_text: Story is I'm not too sure there's anybody they want to do that back to other than me, but I was very privileged. The seniority system isn't a very good system, but that's way ahead of whatever is number two. And so lightning struck twice once with the Freeman Farm Bill back in 96. And that left 40 years of agriculture program policy where the government was telling folks what to do with set-asides and everything else, everything we tried to set aside in the grain sector or soybeans or corn or whatever, weed, coarse sorghum. Our competitors simply increased their production by more than we set aside, plus all of the other stuff that we were telling farmers what to do. And it was a guy named Leon Torline, not in Dodge City, when I would go out there, where you'd go to a breakfast with about 30 of these guys. And I was bemoaning the fact that we couldn't get enough money from the Gingrich troop to really do a farm bill, at least as we have known it. And Leon stood up and said, Pat, why don't we just give it, you know, give me the freedom to farm. He said, I can take care of my own stuff. He says, you just give me some kind of a target price payment or whatever else that you want to deem it. So we called it the market transition payment. It was a direct payment. And then also crop insurance, which we really increased. But farmers could plant whatever they want to plant according to the market. So that was a big one. And then in 2018, when I'd ever seven and I worked together very hard, You have to be bipartisan in a farm bill. And we got 87 votes for that bill. But that was during a time and still is today where farmers have to have farmers ranchers and growers have to have certainty and predictability. That's how we sold it. We had over a thousand different organizations in behalf of that farm bill, which set a record. Very proud of that.
